segments.en: What is clear is what we have already recounted of their use of vessels of gourd. We do not know what their reason in this is, except by way of conjecture and analogy from what has been reported of them. It may be that they agree with the Samaritans in keeping apart from the impurity [contracted] from any of the people; and perhaps too they hold that one who has drawn near a corpse in this age has no purification, since there is no purifying water; and that all the vessels taken from people's hands are impure, so they take vessels of gourd and make them for themselves.

What strengthens this conjecture: one of the reporters reported of them that no other person tells them anything of the reading [of the months?] and the harvest. This too is mysterious, and we do not know what its cause is.

It is also reported of them that they observe Sunday together with the Sabbath. This indicates that they incline to something of the doctrine of the Christians. This is what has reached me of their doctrine, some of which I saw in a book of one of the reporters in the account of the sects.

I had thought that the Qurʿiyya arose after "Jesus" and after Christianity, until I examined a book of "David son of Marwān al-Muqammiṣ" that he calls "Kitāb al-Ḍarāʿa," in which he mentions that the religion of Christianity was taken from the doctrine of the Sadducees and the Qurʿiyya together. This showed that the Qurʿiyya were before Christianity; so, [revising] what I had supposed, I have set their mention [where I did].
